chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Sulayman al-Ja'fari said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father used to fast on the Day of 'Arafah while standing at the station (of 'Arafah) on a hot day, and he would order a high shade to be set up for him, so he would perform ritual bath from the heat that reached him.'

key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Day of 'Arafah, the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah

ai.seo_question: What did the Imams do regarding fasting and cooling down on the Day of 'Arafah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the practical application of *rafah* (exemption from hardship) in the Sunnah, where the Imam himself sought relief from extreme heat during the standing at 'Arafah by using a raised shade and performing ghusl. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that maintaining physical well-being during worship is not only permissible but encouraged, reflecting the balance between spiritual devotion and bodily comfort emphasized in the Ahl al-Bayt's practices.
